title: Agreement with the affine-line route on affine space
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $A=\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ for any $n\geq1$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $d\geq0$, let $p_d:X=\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ be the projection [def-sbc-affine-space], and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use the specified pro-etale twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

The affine comparison at every coefficient level is specified as follows. For an affine-line projection $p:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ with standard compactification $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$, $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, define $I_S:Rp_!A(1)[2]\to A_S$ by $Rq_*j_!A(1)[2]\to Rq_*A(1)[2]\xrightarrow{t_q}A_S$. Here $t_q$ is the ordinary etale projective-line trace [def-amb-p1-trace], formed with $\mu_{\ell^r}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A$ for any $r\geq1$ such that $\ell^rA=0$, and realized on the specified pro-etale Tate twist by [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map, lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Define $\Gamma_{p,K}$ as the exceptional transpose of
$$
Rp_!Lp^*K(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}K\otimes_A^LRp_!A(1)[2]\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes I_S}K,
$$
using the projection map [def-exchange-projection]. These maps are independent of $r$. Put $\Gamma_{p_0,K}=1_K$ and define $\Gamma_{p_d,K}$ as the ordered composite of these $d$ affine-line maps, with the exceptional-composition and twist-additivity isomorphisms as in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]. On the domain $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$ of [def-pur-affine-line-datum], these are exactly the named maps [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison, thm-pur-affine-line-purity, cor-pur-affine-space-purity]; the displayed construction specifies their extension to all $n\geq1$.

Specify the diagonal/DNC normalization in the smooth purity map [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] as follows, as in the model paragraph of the unit. Put $W=X\times_YX$, with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$, and let $\alpha:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_d}$ be [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. Let $N=N_{\Delta/W}$ and let $\delta:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_N,0_N)$ be the normalized comparison [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], with section invariants [def-pur-section-invariant]. On the normal bundle use the inverse of the integration-transposed comparison of [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity], with integration [def-amb-vector-integration], transported by [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Pulling it back along $0_N$ and restricting the twist gives $\beta:C(\pi_N,0_N)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$. The dualizing orientation used in the middle arrow of the smooth purity map is $\vartheta_p=\beta\delta\alpha^{-1}:\omega_p\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$; that middle arrow uses $\vartheta_p^{-1}$.

Then this smooth purity map equals $\Gamma_{p_d,K}$ as a morphism
$$
Lp_d^*K(d)[2d]\longrightarrow Rp_d^!K.
$$
For $d=0$ both maps are $1_K$.

proof.text: Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^r A=0$. Apply [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] to the trivial bundle over each base used here. Its statement gives the coherent specified Tate realization, the equality of the projective-line decompositions and traces, the open-counit restriction to $I_S$, and independence of $r$. Thus the displayed definition of each affine-line $\Gamma$ and its ordered composites is independent of $r$. This cites the coefficient and Kummer comparison as an existing lemma, rather than re-proving it using an empty divisor.

source.place: Returned Step 1: finite coefficient realization and exponent independence

proof.text: For $K$, choose the bounded constructible etale representative $K^e$ of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). By [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) it has the finite Tor interval of $K$, so [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] compares the actual projection/integration transposes on these inputs. Every scheme in the coordinate and projective compactification towers is finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and of finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Their projective compactifications therefore have integer dimension bounds. The source inputs are bounded etale-origin objects, so the Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] apply. Empty schemes have the unique maps between zero objects.

source.place: Returned Step 1: witness, Tor and compactification domains

proof.text: Put $p=p_d$, $X=\mathbf A^d_Y$ and $W=X\times_YX$. The projection $p$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. The diagonal base-change isomorphism is $\alpha:C(p_1,\Delta)\to\omega_p$ of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]; the section invariant is [def-pur-section-invariant]. The diagonal is regular of codimension $d$, with normal bundle $T_{X/Y}$ by [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]. In coordinates $(x,y)$, the isomorphism $h(x,y)=(x,u=y-x)$ has inverse $(x,u)\mapsto(x,x+u)$, takes $\Delta$ to zero, and sends its conormal basis $y_i-x_i$ to $u_i$. Thus its normal-coordinate basis is unchanged. The schemes and morphisms here are separated finite type by their polynomial charts; for $d=0$ the coordinate lists are empty.

source.place: Returned Step 1: diagonal and standard-pair coordinates

proof.text: The extracted lemma [lem-pur-affine-translation-trace], applied over $X$ to the section $(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$, says exactly that $h$ preserves the normalized integration. The actual site and transpose comparisons are [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] and the Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Applying those functors and bijections to the trace equality shows that the integration-transposed comparison is unchanged by $h$. This is the translation argument of the unit model paragraph, including the universal parameter and base-change normalization.

For any rank-$d$ trivial bundle $q$, write $P_{q,K}:Lq^*K(d)[2d]\to Rq^!K$ for the integration transpose, which is invertible by [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] and [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. The integration is [def-amb-vector-integration]. Put $L=A_X(d)[2d]$, $P=P_{p,A_Y}$, $L'=A_W(d)[2d]$, and $J=P_{p_1,A_X}$. Let $B:Lp_2^*\omega_p\to\omega_{p_1}$ be the specified dualizing base-change map. The trace base-change equation is [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], transported by the site comparison just cited. Therefore [lem-pur-trace-transpose-base-change] applied to this square gives $J=B\circ Lp_2^*P$. In [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $\alpha=(L\Delta^*B)^{-1}$ under $p_2\Delta=1_X$, and hence
$$\alpha\circ L\Delta^*J=P.$$
The ordinary Tate restriction $L\Delta^*L'=L$ is the coherent restriction already fixed above.

source.place: Returned Step 3: base change of the integration transpose

proof.text:
Apply [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] to $(p_1,\Delta)$, obtaining $\delta:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_N,0_N)$. In the global coordinates $u_i=y_i-x_i$ this is a standard affine pair. Its deformation is given by $u_i=t v_i$ and has constant family object by the standard-pair clause of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry]. The normalization clause of the DNC theorem makes $\delta$ the identity between these two standard section invariants. Write $\beta=L0_N^*(P_{\pi_N,A_X}^{-1})$, followed by Step 3's ordinary Tate restriction, so $\beta:C(\pi_N,0_N)\to A_X(d)[2d]$. The induced normal coordinates $v_i$ use the same ordered basis as $u_i$, by Step 3. With Step 4's translation invariance, the standard-pair identity says precisely $\beta\delta=(L\Delta^*J)^{-1}$. The explicitly specified diagonal/DNC normalization in the statement and in the middle arrow of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] is $\theta_p=\beta\delta\alpha^{-1}$. By Step 5,
$$\theta_p=(L\Delta^*J)^{-1}\alpha^{-1}=P_{p,A_Y}^{-1}.$$
This checks the actual normalized arrows; it does not deduce equality merely from existence of isomorphisms to a twist. In rank zero the displayed coordinate lists are empty, the deformation is the constant rank-zero pair, and the same equations are identities.

source.place: Proof, standard-pair identity; unit Agreement on the model, final three sentences

proof.text: The two projection maps at $(L,K)$ and $(\omega_p,K)$ used below are invertible by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. Its source coefficients have bounded constructible etale witnesses: $L$ is the realized shifted Tate line, and the previous DNC computation gives $P:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_p$. Its base coefficient is the witness $K^e$ above, with finite Tor interval by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii). The separated finite-type projection $p$ therefore satisfies every hypothesis; no Tor condition on an arbitrary source coefficient or six-functor datum is assumed.

By [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] and the DNC computation, smooth purity is $\theta_{p,K}(1\otimes P)$ after the fixed Tate reassociation. Apply [lem-pur-tensor-trace-transpose] with $t=t_p$ and $L=A_X(d)[2d]$. It identifies this map with the transpose of $(1_K\otimes t_p)\Pi_{L,K}$. This is exactly $P_{p,K}$, by [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] and [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. Thus the smooth map equals the integration transpose for every $K$. The tensor/counit identification is now a separate lemma; it is not inferred from naturality in $K$ alone.

source.place: Returned Step 5: passage from the unit orientation to arbitrary K

proof.text: For the coordinate tower we need projection compatibility as an identity of maps. For $f=q_d:\mathbf A^{d+1}_Y\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ and $g=p_d$, compactify $g$ by $(\mathbf P^1_Y)^d$ and take the compatible compactification triangle for $f$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle]. All these schemes are finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], so the qcqs hypothesis holds and their opens are quasi-compact. The normalized compositor of this triangle is that of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]; at the finite pro-etale level its proper/open interchange is the evaluation in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], and with [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] these are the comparisons defining the compositor $\alpha$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition] on the witnessed inputs.

source.place: Returned Step 6: compatible compactifications and the normalized compositor

proof.text:
For the triangle of the preceding step, [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate] states, for arbitrary ambient finite-coefficient inputs and the counit-defined projection maps of [def-exchange-projection], the identity
$$\operatorname{PF}_{gf;M,N}(\alpha_M\otimes1)
=\alpha_{M\otimes P_fP_gN}\,Rg_!(\operatorname{PF}_{f;M,P_gN})\,\operatorname{PF}_{g;Rf_!M,N},$$
with $P_u=Lu^*$ and the canonical pullback, tensor and direct-image associators inserted. By the preceding step its $\alpha$ is the actual compositor of [thm-sf-comp-composition] on the witnessed inputs used here. No coherence of a six-functor datum is invoked. Clause 3 of [lem-pur-finite-projection-action-laws] gives the tensor-action identity for each compactification projection map.

source.place: Returned Step 6: projection compatibility with the compact-support compositor

proof.text: All inverses in the tower calculation are on the domain of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. The source coefficients are shifted Tate lines or their products, and the affine-line direct image of such a line is $A$ by [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] and [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. Base factors are $K$, its pullbacks, and their tensors with locally free Tate lines. By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] these pullbacks are bounded constructible with the same finite Tor interval; tensor with a locally free line preserves it, and a shift translates it. Etale witnesses exist by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and their Tor intervals are reflected by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii). Thus every application of the preceding tensor-interchange and projection identities has the required witnessed bounded-below and finite-Tor inputs.

source.place: Returned Step 6: domains of all projection inverses and iterated affine-line inputs

proof.text: Work first on the ordinary etale site. For a line projection $q$, [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] identifies the actual projective-line counit at every coefficient $K$ with coefficient tensor the normalized trace after inverse projection. The explicit affine-line adjunction of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] composes it with extension by zero. Its counit is that projective-line counit composed with $Rq_*$ of the open counit. Naturality of the proper projection map in its first variable, applied to the open counit at $A(1)[2]$, and the compatibility of the open tensor isomorphism with the open counit (clause 2 of [lem-pur-finite-projection-action-laws]) identify its coefficient formula with $(1_K\otimes I_S)\Pi$, where $\Pi$ is built from the compactification projection map of [def-exchange-projection] for $c=(j,q)$. The comparison [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] carries precisely this formula and its transpose to the specified pro-etale line map $\Gamma_{q,K}$. On the originally named domain this is [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. The formulas apply at all $n\geq1$ by the exponent independence established above.

source.place: Returned Step 6: the affine-line counit at arbitrary coefficients

proof.text: On the pro-etale site use the explicit affine adjunctions, transported by [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], from the affine adjunctions $F_d\dashv G_d$ of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], where $G_dK=p_d^*K(d)[2d]$. Inductively their counits have the coefficient formula just established in rank one. Apply [lem-pur-composite-integration-counit] to $f=q_d:\mathbf A^{d+1}_Y\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ and $g=p_d$, taking $L_f=A(1)[2]$ and $L_g=A(d)[2d]$. The projection hypotheses are the compositor identity and the compactification tensor-action identity of the preceding steps, on the verified domains. This lemma makes the composite counit $(1_K\otimes t_{p_{d+1}})\Pi$: at the tensor unit it is precisely the trace defining [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], and [def-amb-vector-integration] uses that trace on a trivial bundle. The induction starts from the identity adjunction at $d=0$. Thus the integration transpose $P_{p_d,K}$ is the adjunction-preserving comparison with the ordered composite of the explicit line adjunctions.

source.place: Returned Step 6: coefficient factorization of the ordered composite counit

proof.text:
The composition convention on exceptional functors is the conjugate of $\alpha$ specified in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], using [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Its ordered recursion uses $Rq_d^!Rp_d^!K$ instead of $G_1G_dK$. Naturality of the affine-line transpose gives
$$\Gamma_{q_d,Rp_d^!K}\,Lq_d^*(P_{p_d,K})(1)[2]
=Rq_d^!(P_{p_d,K})\,\Gamma_{q_d,G_dK}.$$
It follows from naturality of the defining projection/integration composite in [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], so substitution identifies the recursion with the composite counit just computed. Here $G_dK$ has the verified finite-Tor domain, and $Rp_d^!K\cong G_dK$ by the earlier integration comparison. The fixed Tate pullback and twist-additivity identifications are those in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]; all shift factors have even degree. Finally [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] carries this counit equality and its transposes to the pro-etale site. Hence $P_{p_d,K}=\Gamma_{p_d,K}$; combined with the earlier DNC calculation this is the desired agreement. In rank zero all maps are $1_K$, and the calculation also covers $K=0$.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions],
for the projection $p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ the smooth purity map
$\gamma_{p_d,K}$ of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] equals the
affinity-space purity comparison of [cor-pur-affine-space-purity],
i.e. the ordered composite of the $d$ affinity-line purity maps of
[thm-pur-affine-line-purity].

proof.text:
Both maps are canonical and, by [thm-pur-composition-coherence]
and [prop-pur-affine-space-purity-compatibilities], they are
compatible with the tower of affine projections. It therefore suffices
to compare them after restriction to a geometric fiber of $Y$, where
both are determined by the Kummer computation: the dualizing-object
identification of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] for $p_d$ comes
from the deformation of the diagonal $\Delta$ and the standard-pair
computation of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](4) – the diagonal
of the standard pair $(\mathbf A^{2d}_Y,\Delta)$ has normal bundle the
trivial rank-$d$ bundle $T_{p_d}$, and the DNC invariance of
[thm-pur-dnc-invariance] is the identity on the standard pair –
whose class, by
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry] and the definition of the
[def-pur-frame-class] (class of a frame), is the $d$-fold
exterior product of the rank-one Kummer boundaries, i.e. the
$d$-fold product of the affinity-line orientations; the affinity-space
purity of [cor-pur-affine-space-purity] is built from exactly the
same $d$-fold product of the affinity-line orientations. The two
assemblies differ only by the canonical reassociations of the package
(the Koszul signs are $+1$, since all shift factors are of even
degree, by [prop-pur-affine-space-purity-compatibilities]); hence
the maps agree.
